newsitem.title: UK: IWCC sets up group to consider SIB metal review.
newsitem.headline: IWCC sets up group to consider SIB metal review.

text.p: The International Wrought Copper Council (IWCC) has set up a group to consider the recent document by the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), and in a due course will make a formal response.

In its annual report (1995/96) the IWCC said the SIB review of the metal markets provides the industry with an opportunity to put forward detailed proposals and ideas for improvements in the operation of the London Metal Exchange (LME).
The LME needs a strong industrial basis to its contracts, good liquidity not susceptible to undue influence by a handful of operators and a balance between flexibility and regulation.
The IWCC also said it is important to keep some of the major and unique advantages of the LME, such as credit clearing.
It added that these issues are important to the LME's future, and they are not to do with losses incurred by a particular operator.
This investigation is for the regulators, and issues of corporate governance should not be confused with the governance of the LME, the IWCC said.
"The key question is whether the LME's systems of self-regulation and of maintaining an orderly market are sufficient to cope with potential manipulation," it said.

The IWCC noted that no new delivery locations were created during the year. However, Los Angeles/Long Beach will be split into two separate locations - the latter area receiving considerable throughput.

"While it is true that a broader spread of delivery points can help to mitigate backwardations by facilitating delivery of metal, certain locations can also provide an additional tool for manipulating the market," it said.
Plans to create new delivery locations should be discussed widely and openly with all interested parties, the IWCC said.
